answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network enforces an escrow terrace where each identity locks 500 scarce tokens for 20 epochs and submits a physical crystal clock-drift proof from distinct hardware. Influence and task rewards scale sublinearly via square-root curves across verified accounts. An attacker creating N identities must lock 500*N non-reusable tokens, yet sublinear payouts bound total rewards below the opportunity cost of capital. Splitting stake across compliant nodes in the lotus cluster yields diminishing returns, making bulk identity replication strictly unprofitable.
